articles.title: Amarius Mims draws All-Pro buzz after dominant Bengals performance
articles.summary: Bengals right tackle Amarius Mims allowed zero pressures over 37 pass-blocking snaps in Cincinnati’s Week 1 win over Tampa Bay.
articles.body:
Cincinnati Bengals right tackle Amarius Mims certainly came to strut his stuff in the Bengals ' season opener.

Mims arrived with breakout expectations, and his season opener surfaced hopeful signs of more than solid play to come.

He allowed zero pressures across 37 pass-blocking snaps in Cincinnati's 33-27 win over the Tampa Bay Buccaneers on Sunday, according to Gridiron Grading , citing Pro Football Focus' initial charting.

The account noted that Mims primarily matched up against Buccaneers rookie edge rusher Rueben Bain Jr. and added that the performance would represent the highest pass-blocking grade of Mims' career if the initial grading is true.

"Amarius Mims looks like an All-Pro," Gridiron Grading wrote in an earlier post. "He's about to make the leap."

Mims, Cincinnati's No. 18 overall pick in the 2024 NFL draft, has flashed high-end ability throughout his young career when healthy.

Supposing Sunday's initial numbers hold, his third NFL season is off to about as strong a start as Cincinnati could have hoped.

articles.title: Marcelo Gallardo, nuevo seleccionador de Ecuador
articles.standfirst: Gallardo ocupará el cargo que hasta el Mundial de Norteamérica ocupó su compatriota Sebastián Beccacece
articles.summary: Gallardo ocupará el cargo que hasta el Mundial de Norteamérica ocupó su compatriota Sebastián Beccacece
articles.body: El argentino Marcelo Gallardo es el nuevo seleccionador elegido por la Federación Ecuatoriana de Fútbol (FEF) para dirigir la Tri. La contratación del exjugador y ex entrenador de River Plate le plantea dos desafíos específicos: una gran campaña en la Copa América de 2028 y la clasificación para el Mundial de 2030. Gallardo ocupará el cargo que hasta el Mundial de Norteamérica ocupó su compatriota Sebastián Beccacece. Becccacece dirigió a la Tri hasta su eliminación en los dieciseisavos de final del Mundial 2026. "Tenemos talento, estructura y ambición. Estamos listos", anunció este domingo la FEF al anunciar la contratación a través de su cuenta de X. "Que la gente crea, porque tiene qué creer. Bienvenido Marcelo", manifestó el presidente de la Federación Ecuatoriana de Fútbol, Francisco Egas. El directivo expresó que Gallardo "hizo de la exigencia una manera de entender el fútbol, la obsesión por competir, por mejorar y por no conformarse". Agregó que el entrenador, nacido hace 50 años en Merlo, se ha caracterizado por "construir equipos que crean, que estén preparados para los grandes momentos, que ganen y al día siguiente vuelvan a pensar en ganar". "Ecuador también viene construyendo su camino, tenemos una generación que compite al máximo nivel, tenemos talento, estructura y ambición", afirmó Egas. "Creemos que esta selección está preparada para dar el salto, para exigirse más, para competir por más, por eso fuimos a buscar a Marcelo Gallardo, por lo que ganó, pero por sobre todo por lo que representa", agregó el directivo. El primer desafío de Gallardo será el partido amistoso contra Corea del Sur el 24 de septiembre en el estadio Suwon World Cup de la ciudad surcoreana de Suwon. El segundo partido de preparación del equipo suramericano será contra Japón el 1 de octubre en el estadio de Yokohama, y cerrará su gira contra el ganador del partido entre Nueva Zelanda y Panamá en el estadio Nacional de Tokio. Ecuador participará desde el próximo año en las eliminatorias sudamericanas para el Mundial de 2030, y entre junio y julio de 2028 esta prevista la disputa de la Copa América, en sede que debe confirmar la Conmebol. Ecuador ha participado en los Mundiales de Corea del Sur y Japón 2002, Alemania 2006, Brasil 2014, Catar 2022 y el disputado este año en Estados Unidos, México y Canadá.

articles.title: Mueren en accidente de moto el guardaespaldas de la novia de Vinicius y su esposa: "Tengo el corazón roto"
articles.standfirst: La infuencer Virgínia Fonseca confirmó en su cuenta de Instagram los fallecimientos de Rogério Camilo Ramos y Paulla Regina Rodarte Camilo
articles.summary: La infuencer Virgínia Fonseca confirmó en su cuenta de Instagram los fallecimientos de Rogério Camilo Ramos y Paulla Regina Rodarte Camilo
articles.body: La influencer Virgínia Fonseca, que junto a su novio Vinicius (Real Madrid), fue protagonista en el circuito de Madring durante el Gran Premio de España de Fórmula 1. Horas después la pareja del futbolista del Real Madrid informó en su cuenta de Instagram que su guardaespaldas, Rogério Camilo Ramos, y su esposa, Paulla Regina Rodarte Camilo, murieron en un accidente de tráfico en Brasil. "Gente, hace un rato recibí la noticia sobre Camilo (nuestro guardia de seguridad personal) y su esposa; no había publicado nada antes porque esperábamos a que todos los familiares se enteraran, pero desde que recibí la noticia no he podido hacer nada más, tengo el corazón roto", publicó Virgínia en Instagram. Rogério Camilo Ramos y Paulla Regina Rodarte Camilo fallecieron en un accidente de moto en la carretera BR-060, en la zona de Ribeirao da Posse, municipio de Guapó (Región Metropolitana de Goiania). 'Rota Verde Goiás' informa que el accidente ocurrió en el kilómetro 201 de la vía, en sentido sur. La muerte de Rogério, quien conducía la motocicleta, fue confirmada por la médica de Rota Verde Goiás a las 9:02 a. m. Paulla Regina, fue encontrada en parada cardiorrespiratoria y recibió asistencia con el apoyo del Cuerpo de Bomberos, pero no sobrevivió. "Camilo, te estaremos eternamente agradecidos por todo el cuidado, la protección, la sabiduría, la pureza y el amor inmenso que siempre dedicaste a nuestra familia. Tu presencia era un refugio seguro y tu recuerdo vivirá para siempre en nuestros corazones", se despidió la pareja de Vinícius. "Gente, hace un rato recibí la noticia sobre Camilo (nuestro guardia de seguridad personal) y su esposa; no había publicado nada antes porque esperábamos a que todos los familiares se enteraran, pero desde que recibí la noticia no he podido hacer nada más, tengo el corazón roto. La vida es, de hecho, un suspiro, y en este momento de tristeza las palabras parecen insuficientes, sobre todo ante cosas que nunca llegaremos a comprender; sólo nos queda confiar en el propósito de Dios. Camilo, te estaremos eternamente agradecidos por todo el cuidado, la protección, la sabiduría, la pureza y el amor inmenso que siempre dedicaste a nuestra familia. Tu presencia era un refugio seguro y tu recuerdo vivirá para siempre en nuestros corazones. Sabemos que, ahora, tú y Paula serán los ángeles de la guarda de la pequeña Heloísa, velando por ella desde allá arriba. Aquí abajo, nos uniremos a la familia para garantizar que ella nunca se sienta desamparada, cuidándola con todo el cariño que ustedes siempre transmitieron. Que Dios consuele el corazón de todos los familiares y, de manera especial, el de Heloísa. Mis más sinceras condolencias".

articles.title: SDFC handed heavy 5-0 defeat at home by Philadelphia Union
articles.summary: San Diego FC’s Sunday night ends in a 5-0 unravelling loss against the Philadelphia Union on Hispanic Heritage Night at Snapdragon Stadium.
articles.body:
SAN DIEGO -- San Diego FC 's Sunday night ends in a 5-0 unravelling loss against the Philadelphia Union on Hispanic Heritage Night at Snapdragon Stadium.

SDFC were back at home for their 25th matchday of the 2026 MLS Regular Season, hosting interconference side Philadelphia Union to mark the two clubs' first-ever meeting.

Coming off a midweek 1-0 losing effort against in-state rival San Jose Earthquakes on Wednesday night that snapped a five-match winning streak at Snapdragon Stadium, SDFC looked to bounce back in front of their fans to remain in contention for an MLS Cup playoff spot.

They enter Sunday's matchday sitting in the ninth and final Western Conference postseason place, right in front of the trailing tenth-place LA Galaxy , all level on points but holding the tiebreaker advantage due to total wins in the campaign.

SDFC's biggest change to their starting XI came at the goalkeeper position, with Duran Ferree in between the sticks against the Union as usual starter CJ dos Santos was suspended after picking up a second yellow against the Earthquakes last time out.

After a cagey first 45 minutes and what looked to be headed for a scoreless tie into the halftime break, the match caught fire in the closing first-half minutes with a shown red card and goal.

Directly following a foul on former SDFC, now Philadelphia Union forward Milan Iloski , midfielder Alejandro Alvarado seemingly fired the ball directly into the face of the going-down Iloski, which triggered referee Ismail Elfath to show the SDFC player a straight red card in the 45-minute.

The ensuing VAR check on the incident showed the accidental but unnecessary kick of the ball, with referee Elfath downgrading Alvarado's booking to a yellow card, as SDFC avoided going down to ten men in back-to-back games.

Then it was the Union that broke the deadlock in the 45+5-minute, coming off a moment of magic from 16-year-old American sensation Cavan Sullivan , letting off a goal-area backheel flick across goal, off the far right post and into the net for the 1-0 lead.

SDFC closed out the first half dominating possession, but fell short in shots and goal creation, with the Union tripling the Chrome & Azuls' four total shots.

The Sullivan show continued in the second half, doubling up his goal tally and the Union's lead in the 62-minute after being played in behind into the penalty box as he snuck a low driven shot through the legs of SDFC's Ferree at the left sided near post for the 2-0 score and his brace.

Only five minutes later, Philadelphia added their third to the match with an attack involving Sullivan once again.

Starting with an over-the-top ball into the right wing space from Sullivan, Iloski got his revenge against his former side as he assisted Bruno Damiani with a pass near the center of the penalty area as Damiani got the finishing touch in the 67-minute to make it 3-0.

The bad luck continued for SDFC with midfielder Anibal Godoy finding his own net in the 87-minute, heading the ball back and over Duran Ferree for the fourth Philadelphia goal.

The Union managed to add a fifth and final goal in the final minute of added stoppage time to the second half, with forward Malik Jakupovic getting on the end of a goal-area tap-in finish in the 90+4-minute that sealed the 5-0 scoreline at Snapdragon Stadium.

Following the home loss to Philadelphia, SDFC head coach Mikey Varas spoke on his team's recent lack of consistency and the changes coming within the group.

"Ultimately, this is an unacceptable situation, an unacceptable result. I take full responsibility at the end of the day. It's my job to get the group ready to play."

"And for whatever reason, this group has not found any sort of consistency. But what I can promise is we're gonna go back to the drawing board, and we're gonna make the environment even more competitive."

"Because these guys gotta fight for their lives if they want to be here, and they gotta show a lot more than what they're showing."

"It's just not who we are. We can say that it's a blip on the radar, but we take these blips very seriously. So we need to self-correct, very quickly, because it's unacceptable."

It's been an unfortunate run of matches for San Diego FC, having fallen in their last three games, including Sunday's 5-0 loss to the Union that marked the club's biggest margin of defeat.

SDFC moves away from MLS play this Wednesday night, hosting cross-border rivals Club Tijuana on Sept. 16 at Snapdragon Stadium for the second-ever Baja Cup, with kickoff set for 7 p.m.

The Chrome & Azul recently took down the Xolos back on August 9, with 18-year-old forward Bryan Zamblé's 22-minute goal being enough to seal the 1-0 Leagues Cup victory at home.

articles.title: Giants at Rams Week 2 opening odds: Giants open as big underdogs
articles.summary: The NY Giants open as heavy underdogs against the Los Angeles Rams
articles.body:
The New York Giants open Week 2 as 8.5-point underdogs on the road against the Los Angeles Rams , per F anDuel Sportsbook .

The Giants opened their season by stunning the Dallas Cowboys , but have an uphill battle ahead of them against the Rams in Week 2 on Monday Night Football.

This game was widely expected to be a blowout win for the Rams, but it's significantly more complicated than it appeared when the schedule first came out.

First the Rams decision to travel to Australia shortly before their season opener rather than arrive early seemed to backfire. They appeared gassed from the start against the San Francisco 49ers and were outplayed by their division rival. Then the Rams learned earlier Sunday that star pass rusher Myles Garret would need knee surgery and will spend (at least) the next four weeks on the short-term injured reserve.

It remains to be seen in what condition the Rams will be after travelling back from Australia to the

The Giants, meanwhile, are riding high after a dominating 28-20 victory over the Cowboys on Sunday Night Football. The Giants utterly controlled the line of scrimmage and time of possession, running the ball down the Cowboys' throat while Jaxson Dart was surgical with the football.

Can the Giants travel across the country and turn their Week 1 win into an actual winning streak?

articles.title: El Barça se adueña del balón: más de 700 pases por partido
articles.standfirst: También está dominando la posesión
articles.summary: También está dominando la posesión
articles.body: El Barcelona está lanzado en este inicio de la temporada en todas las facetas del juego. El bloque culé está teniendo la posesión de la pelota de forma muy clara pero, además, está teniendo paciencia a la hora de atacar. Los azulgranas tocan el balón buscando espacios. Muestra de ello es que en los últimos tres encuentros disputados, contra Valencia, Feyenoord y Levante, ha superado las 700 combinaciones. En Valencia, los azulgranas firmaron 728 pases y en el estreno en la máxima competición europea, contra el Feyenoord, 746. En el Ciutat de València, la estadística se mantuvo en esta línea y los culés firmaron 711 combinaciones. Además, destaca que en los primeros cinco minutos, antes del gol de Xavi Espart, el Levante apenas tocó el esférico y el Barcelona hizo circular la pelota, similar a lo que podría ser un rondo. Los culés arrancaron la temporada con 463 pases en el choque en Elche, 560 contra el Athletic y 585, contra el Rayo Vallecano. Pero es en los últimos tres compromisos cuando culés aún han demostrado más poder asociativo. Habrá que ver si mantiene esta dinámica contra el Racing el miércoles. En el Ciutat de València el Barcelona firmó la mayor posesión de la temporada. Los catalanes tuvieron un 75 por ciento, superando el 74 del campo del Valencia y el 72 del choque contra el Feyenoord de Champions. Por lo tanto, los números de los tres últimos partidos demuestran que el Barça sigue en línea ascendente en este arranque

articles.title: Cavan's epic brace, Nashville's Shield grip & more from Matchday 26
articles.summary: By Charles BoehmMLS Matchday 26 featured 15 games involving all 30 clubs.Yet in its wake, two words above all will be on the lips of soccer likers across Nor...
articles.body:
MLS Matchday 26 featured 15 games involving all 30 clubs.

Yet in its wake, two words above all will be on the lips of soccer likers across North America and beyond: Cavan Sullivan .

The Philadelphia Union' s wunderkind struck again out in Southern California on Sunday Night Soccer presented by Continental Tire, extending his – and his team's – remarkable run of form, and cranking up the volume on his US men's national team prospects as we count down to Mauricio Pochettino's release of the Yanks' roster for the upcoming FIFA international window.

No surprise that we'll start our whiparound at Snapdragon Stadium.

Philly's 16-year-old phenom had perhaps the most impressive outing of his fledgling MLS career on Sunday, notching his first MLS brace and adding an assist for good measure as the Union utterly smashed San Diego FC , 5-0 .

And these were no run-of-the-mill finishes, either.

Now, we're not about to call him the American Messi or anything rash like that. Peep the statistics, though: both Sullivan (5g/7a) and Lionel Messi (7g/5a) have racked up 12 goal contributions in their last seven games. That's the GOAT, the two-time defending Landon Donovan MLS MVP we're talking about.

There's an understandable sentiment to be cautious about Cavan, to pump the brakes on the hype train that so often gathers behind highly talented North American prospects when they catch our attention. Pochettino himself did much the same, albeit without mentioning anyone by name, when he spoke with reporters on Labor Day.

But, look: The younger of the Union's Sullivan siblings is doing stuff we've never seen from a teenager in MLS, week in, week out. And it's powering a legit Lazarus act by his team, who are now 8W-0L-2D since the FIFA World Cup pause, looking not so much like an Audi MLS Cup Playoffs qualifier as a legit dark-horse title threat.

Herons held again in top-of-the-table tussle

Nu Stadium witnessed a No. 1 vs No. 2 showdown between Nashville SC and Inter Miami CF on Walmart Saturday Showdown, a clash that crackled with quality and intensity – and it might just have given us a preview of the Eastern Conference final as well.

This was two heavyweights trading haymakers, "a big boys' game," in the words of NSH head coach B.J. Callaghan. Sam Surridge struck early for the visitors. Miami counterpunched viciously and seemed to have a grasp on all three points when Lionel Messi netted his MLS Golden Boot presented by Audi-leading 19th goal of the season just past the hour mark.

The Coyotes had one more sting left in the tail, though. After solid work from supersub Shak Mohammed , Surridge poached expertly to snatch the 2-2 leveler in second-half stoppage time, sniffing out a rebound at the back post to steal yet another two points from the Herons in their own house. With a 3W-2L-6D record at Nu, IMCF have now taken just 15 of the 33 points available to them at their glittering new home.

As a result, what could've been a dire week for Nashville – who got ambushed by Toronto FC at midweek – got a lot less ugly. NSH's lead over their closest Supporters' Shield pursuers, Vancouver and Miami, shrunk a bit, yes, yet remains healthy: eight and nine points, respectively.

One of the weekend's most unhinged games unfolded at TQL Stadium, and yes, you've heard that before. FC Cincinnati and opportunistic Charlotte FC traded haymakers for 90-plus minutes before Kévin Denkey 's injury-time equalizer imposed a 3-3 deadlock in the end. Also, don't miss the Squirrelinho content .

As dramatic as the finish was, Denkey 's non-celebration speaks volumes about the hosts' overall discontent. Head coach Pat Noonan described it as "a shame" to have dropped points again despite a superior expected goals tally, while goalscorer Pavel Bucha was even blunter, pointing out that "you cannot concede three goals and think about winning the game."

One of MLS's top defenses last season, where they finished second in the Supporters' Shield race, Cincy have now grown perilously leaky. FCC have conceded a whopping 12 goals in their last three games, which leaves them on 59 goals allowed this season, a generous 2.46 per game, level with last-place Sporting KC .

It's probably no coincidence that the Orange & Blue have, according to multiple media reports and the player himself , parted ways with Matt Miazga , the cornerstone of their back line for the last three-plus years and a victim of some serious injury woes, a few months before the expiration of his contract.

Speaking of that bottom-dwelling SKC side, after losing six of their last seven games, during which time they've continued to flirt with some of the worst statistics in the league's history, they pulled off the shock result of the weekend, knocking off star-studded LAFC , 3-1 .

It all started with an absolute banger from their new record signing , André Luiz :

Take note, however, of how the Midwesterners soon doubled their lead: via Taylor Calheira , a standout in the USL Championship acquired by Kansas City last year for far, far, far less than the $18 million Luiz reportedly cost. That's a reminder of the massive importance of under-the-radar and value signings for competitiveness in contemporary MLS. Shout-out to Sporting goalkeeper Stefan Cleveland as well; his seven saves were crucial in staving off the Angelenos' furious second-half rally.

"The problem is, in the first half we stayed on the plane," lamented LAFC boss Marc Dos Santos, whose team have won just once in eight league matches since the start of August. "In the first half we were still in LA, maybe. Very disappointing."

One more note from this upset: The numbers suggest SKC defender Wyatt Meyer , a depth signing from Nashville over the winter, has quietly become a vital cog in their rebuild.

The terminally online among us may have noticed Antoine Griezmann 's visceral discomfort with central Florida's uniquely ferocious summer blend of heat and humidity birthed a hilarious internet meme last week. All that sweat hasn't slowed down Orlando City 's incredible surge, though.

With a six-point week that runs their winning streak to three straight games, Grizi and the Lions just keep cruising. They were markedly superior to their Southern rivals Atlanta United in a 3-2 victory on Wednesday, then committed a bit of highway robbery as Toronto visited Inter.co Stadium on Saturday, seizing the lead via Griezmann near the halfway point and countering the Canadians to death down the stretch for a 3-0 W that made a mockery of TFC's expected-goals superiority.

"They killed us in the right moments," observed new Reds midfielder Niklas Dorsch . "Even when it was 1-0 for Orlando, a lot of chances for us in the end. Orlando today was more killer than us."

That starts with Grizi, who also scored twice at midweek and is now up to 8g/3a in just 10 MLS appearances, though it's also a credit to homegrown attacker Justin Ellis , who's notched assists in four straight games, and the Lions' speed in transition via the likes of Iván Angulo and Tyrese Spicer .

St. Louis CITY SC paid tribute to local icon Tina Turner with their gold away kits this year, and as their unbeaten streak rolls onward like the Mississippi River that flows a mile and a half east of Energizer Park, powering a steady climb up the standings, it feels only right to call back to her memorable hit 'Proud Mary.'

With Saturday's emphatic 4-2 home win over struggling Minnesota United , the Ravioli Boyz have now gone 16 matches across all competitions without tasting defeat – and may even be shifting into a higher gear, just in time for Wednesday's US Open Cup semifinal date with Colorado , where a win will take them to the doorstep of the oldest trophy in the United States.

Pricey summer signings Carlo Holse and Rafa Navarro each produced two goal contributions in this one, the latter bagging his second straight brace, as STL continue to tweak their usual 3-4-2-1 shape to incorporate two out-and-out strikers up top. What's your favorite, Holse's curler or Rafa's delicate chip?

The Loons, meanwhile, keep sinking. They've won just one league match since early May and now sit 12th in the West, looking bereft of ideas or inspiration. Their fun fling with James Rodríguez back in the spring feels like a different era entirely.

Are Austin FC making a postseason push? The Verde & Black stunned West leaders Vancouver on Sunday with a 2-1 smash-and-grab road win , their third in three visits to the Cascadia clubs, led by some astonishingly efficient finishing from veteran striker Christian Ramírez .

How efficient? We're talking four shots for the entire team, two of them on target, both of them icily clinical strikes from the guy they call 'Superman.'

Factoring in their run to the Leagues Cup quarterfinals, ATXFC have now lost just twice in 11 overall matches over the past month and are only one point below the Audi MLS Cup Playoffs line despite a dismal start to the season.

The most valuable result of the weekend might just have been New York City FC 's 2-0 win at Real Salt Lake , a hard-earned win at high altitude that snaps a seven-game winless skid and, the Pigeons hope, turns the page on a dog-days swoon of just one win in 10 across all comps.

articles.title: Dembélé responde a Mbappé en plena lucha por el Balón de Oro: "Nunca he sido el elegido"
articles.standfirst: El delantero del PSG coincide con la opinión del futbolista del Real Madrid sobre que a él siempre se le vio como "un jugador con talento" y a Kylian como "el elegido"
articles.summary: El delantero del PSG coincide con la opinión del futbolista del Real Madrid sobre que a él siempre se le vio como "un jugador con talento" y a Kylian como "el elegido"
articles.body: Ousmane Dembélé, vigente ganador del Balón de Oro, fue preguntado por 'Ligue 1 +' sobre la votaciones para el galardón que debe entregar 'France Football' el 21 de octubre al mejor futbolista del mundo de la temporada "Siempre he estado en el fondo de la clase trabajando duro. A lo largo de toda mi carrera no he dicho ni una palabra; he trabajado muchísimo", dijo el ex del Barça tras el triunfo del PSG por 0-1 ante el Brest en la cuarta jornada de la Ligue 1 con gol del español Ferran Torres. Dembélé, que reconoció que no tiene presión por ganar el Balón de Oro, dejó un comentario que ha generado diferentes juicios en Francia: "Como ya he dicho, nunca me vieron como el elegido, pero me esforcé y el año pasado me vi recompensado con una temporada fantástica en el PSG; y ahora, este año, ya veremos: sin presión, con tranquilidad". El futbolista francés tiene contundentes argumentos para ganar el Balón de Oro 2026 y revalidar su galardón: ganó su segunda Champions League consecutiva, fue decisivo en las eliminatorias antes Liverpool y Bayern y en la final ante el Arsena, ganó la Liga francesa, fue nombrado mejor jugador de la liga francesa y marcó seis goles en el Mundial. El diario 'L'Equipe' destaca que "el elegido" utilizado por Ousmane Dembélé recuerda a unas declaraciones de Kylian Mbappé en 'France Football' en las que el delantero del Real Madrid declaró que "¿Dembélé? Él siempre se le vio como un jugador con talento. A mí, en cambio, siempre se me vio como el elegido". "Yo alcancé la cima enseguida, muy pronto. Ousmane tuvo una trayectoria diferente, marcada por las lesiones, ¡pero ha sabido resarcirse!", explicó Mbappé.

articles.title: Jesús Calleja explica el accidente de Cristóbal Soria haciendo rafting: "Necesitó cinco puntos"
articles.summary: Jesús Calleja explicó el accidente que sufrió Cristóbal Soria, legendario exdelegado del Sevilla y colaborador del programa 'El Chiringuito', durante la grabación el programa 'Planeta Calleja'.
articles.body: Jesús Calleja explicó el accidente que sufrió Cristóbal Soria, legendario exdelegado del Sevilla y colaborador del programa 'El Chiringuito', durante la grabación el programa 'Planeta Calleja'. Cristóbal Soria necesito cinco puntos de sutura tras darse un golpe con un remo haciendo rafting en Costa Rica. articles.title: Palo de Abelardo a Lamine Yamal: "No me ha gustado que haya dicho eso del Balón de Oro"
articles.standfirst: "Lo puedes pensar pero no decir. Creo que no, porque quedas mal"
articles.summary: "Lo puedes pensar pero no decir. Creo que no, porque quedas mal"
articles.body: Abelardo Fernández, futbolista del F.C. Barcelona de 1994 a 2002 que fue 54 veces internacional con España, se mostró muy crítico con Lamine Yamal por las declaraciones del joven delantero del Barça en el programa 'Universo Valdano'. "Yo creo que este año el Balón de Oro me lo merecería yo, por lo que he ganado", le dijo Lamine Yamal a Jorge Valdano en MovistarPlus+. Lamine Yamal compartió que "¿A quién se lo daría yo? Al mejor jugador del mundo. ¿A quién se lo van a dar? Eso ya es una conversación muy larga... Yo creo, sinceramente, que los mejores del mundo somos dos y este año me lo merecería yo por lo que he ganado. Para mí, somos Mbappé y yo los dos mejores del mundo. Para mí está claro y todo el mundo que ve los partidos lo sabe". 'El Pitu' Abelardo no dudó en reconocer en el programa 'Radioestadio Noche' que "eso lo puedes pensar pero no decir. Creo que no, porque quedas mal". "No transmites nada positivo en ese aspecto. Creo que lo puedes pensar y puedes decir, 'hombre, yo puedo estar entre los favoritos, pero estos premios nunca se sabe a quién se los dan...'", opinó el exfutbolista de 56 años. Abelardo le reconoció a Edu Pidal que "no me ha gustado que Lamine Yamal haya dicho eso, igual que el otro día Kylian Mbappé en su entrevista tampoco me gustó". "No me ha gustado que Lamine Yamal haya dicho eso", insistió el exentrenador de Candás, Tuilla, Sporting, Alavés, Espanyol y Cartagena. Abelardo subrayó que "a Messi, que ha sido el Dios del fútbol, nunca le he escuchado decir eso".

articles.title: El pecado capital de Ron Gourlay en el mercado del Valencia: la velocidad de las negociaciones, su principal enemigo
articles.standfirst: Al ya exCEO le faltó agilidad en el mercado: el proceso era claro en la elección de piezas, en definir a por quién se iba pero después llegaba la negociación que ha sido 'una a una' y lentas
articles.summary: Al ya exCEO le faltó agilidad en el mercado: el proceso era claro en la elección de piezas, en definir a por quién se iba pero después llegaba la negociación que ha sido 'una a una' y lentas
articles.body: Un club de fútbol, hoy en día, requiere de una velocidad de crucero cuando se está en el mercado porque si no el de al lado te adelanta sin pestañear y al Valencia le ha faltado mucha agilidad negociadora. Ese convencimiento, ese saber estar en operaciones que ha ido dejando que se cocieran a una potencia tan débil que ha ido en detrimento del club. Y es lo más grave de esta situación. El CEO del Valencia, Ron Gourlay, era el único encargado de negociar, en ese tramo final de todo el proceso y cerrar operaciones, pero éstas han sido demasiado lentas. Le aturullaba lleva en curso varias negociaciones al mismo tiempo. Fallo capital en el fútbol de hoy. Ese fue el principio del fin para el escocés que no ha podido soportar la última embestida cuando él pensaba que poniendo la cabeza de su secretaría técnica a merced de la destitución se salvaría del cargo, pero esta estrategia no le ha servido. Pero lo más llamativo no ha sido esta circunstancia. Lo que más ha influido en el debe de este mercado del Valencia ha sido cómo se han eternizado las mismas. Y lo que ha marcado la diferencia entre el modelo del Valencia y el resto de clubes es que no se han llevado varias operaciones en paralelo sino que se acometían de forma individual. Primero una y cuando se llegara a un acuerdo o no, a por la siguiente. Esta es la velocidad a la que no se puede ir en el mercado de hoy en día y ha ocurrido en el Valencia. Le ha perjudicado. Los mercados en el fútbol actual requieren de 'multinegociaciones' y Ron Gourlay no ha sabido llevar esa gestión. Este ha sido el pecado capital cuando el CEO escocés ha entrado en las fase finales de las operaciones para negociar. Se han eternizado... y lo más llamativo es que no se han llevado varias al unísono. Todo el mercado ha sido monotemático. Primero una, luego otra... y más tarde la siguiente. Porque nombres ha habido encima de la mesa según qué posiciones se necesitaban. Estaba hecho el trabajo bajo la premisa del poco dinero que había en caja para acometer operaciones, se han tratado de ajustar los parámetros en futbolistas que cupiesen dentro de esas normas u obligaciones que habían dispuesto desde Singapur. Pero después las negociaciones se han hecho eternas. Y esa falta de agilidad ha llevado a un estancamiento en el mercado para los intereses del club de Mestalla. A todo ello el descontrol mostrado internamente en la parcela deportiva ha sido el motivo por el que los Lim han decidido prescindir de sus servicios a cualquier coste.

articles.title: Nations League: How is NI squad shaping up for quadruple-header?
articles.summary: Northern Ireland will face four Nations League games in 11 days later this month with injuries, summer switches and individual form all making for an interesting selection when Michael O'Neill names his panel on Tuesday.
articles.body:
Before changes to the international calendar brought in for this season, Northern Ireland would previously have already played their first two fixtures by this stage of September.

Under the new fixture list, manager Michael O'Neill will name a squad on Tuesday for a four-game window, beginning with an away trip to Georgia on 25 September and concluding at home to the same opposition on 5 October. In between they face Hungary in Belfast and Ukraine in Slovakia.

While not quite unprecedented - NI faced four Nations League games in 11 days during the summer of 2022 - the condensed schedule will certainly be a challenge for Northern Ireland and other countries with smaller population bases.

Unfortunately for O'Neill, injuries have already disrupted his plans too.

Using international football to reignite Premier League dreams

O'Neill 'hopeful' training centre plans progress

Star player Conor Bradley has not featured for club or country since knee surgery in January and O'Neill told BBC Sport NI this month that he always suspected the injury "was going to take longer than maybe some people were thinking" before adding it would be a "bonus" to see him in a green jersey before March 2027.

The 23-year-old has missed six of Northern Ireland's past 14 games through injury, and another thanks to a one-game suspension, but in many ways it has been a case of trying to replace the irreplaceable.

The Liverpool full-back tends to play in a more advanced role for his national side on the right-side of a 3-5-2 and, while O'Neill has other natural options for down the flank, none possess the same mix of attacking drive and defensive instinct.

Nor is Bradley the only injury concern before the squad announcement.

Midfielder Ali McCann injured his hamstring in Preston's 4-0 Carabao Cup defeat by Everton last month with his now former club manager Paul Heckingbottom saying his captain would be out for "months".

O'Neill has previously spoken about how the 26-year-old is the sort of player whose importance is highlighted in his absence and his injury leaves a hole in the starting XI alongside Fulham's Shea Charles in the preferred double-pivot.

Injuries leave O'Neill with plenty to ponder

The summer transfer window has again been a busy one for O'Neill's squad with a number of players making moves either on a permanent or loan basis.

Justin Devenny's Stoke career got off to a flying start with a double on his first start since his switch from Crystal Palace. A natural left-footer, he has given NI balance as a wing-back since his debut in June 2025.

A versatile player, Devenny has been turning out as a central midfielder for the Potters and could be one to fill the void left by McCann, as he did in the World Cup play-off defeat by Italy in March.

Oxford United's Brodie Spencer, if he is not needed to replace Bradley on the right, would then be an option to step into the left-wing back role.

Deploying Devenny's new club-mate Ethan Galbraith in a deeper midfield role is another option, one with the added benefit of getting the former Swansea City player on the ball with more frequency.

With Isaac Price sure to fill one of the more advanced midfield positions, using Galbraith elsewhere would then leave O'Neill with a decision to make regarding the slot beside the West Brom man.

Jamie Donley has started as a centre-forward in the side's past five games, scoring against Luxembourg and Wales since first being deployed as a nine, and it feels unlikely he would be moved into a deeper role now.

Patrick Kelly and Callum Marshall are options, but could O'Neill be tempted to throw an exciting but unproven attacking talent in at the deep end?

Liverpool's Kieran Morrison, spending the season on loan at Sheffield Wednesday, Arsenal's Ceadach O'Neill and Braiden Graham of Everton, were all part of the squad in June with the former pair making their international bow in the friendly victory over Guinea.

O'Neill, who drew praise from Mikel Arteta during pre-season , also appeared off the bench against France four days later.

While competitive internationals would be a step up, Michael O'Neill has never been shy to give young players an opportunity before they have established themselves fully at club level.

Four-game window sure to be test of depth

Nobody connected with Northern Ireland will have fond memories of when the side last faced so congested a fixture list.

As a consequence of the Covid-19 pandemic, the June 2022 window similarly contained four games, with then manager Ian Baraclough presiding over losses to Greece and Kosovo, as well as a pair of draws with Cyprus.

Indeed, if not for an added-time equaliser from Jonny Evans against the Cypriots at Windsor Park, results would have been worse.

There is little doubt that such a schedule places greater demands on countries with fewer playing resources.

While, with everyone fit, there was a sense during the last Nations League campaign that O'Neill had settled upon his favoured starting XI, a trio of friendlies so far this year have given him the chance to assess further options.

In four games in 2026, O'Neill has used 27 players, including 21 in the game against Guinea alone.

Like Bradley, Sunderland's Daniel Ballard has not played for the side in this calendar year through injury, while the likes of Dion Charles, Bailey Peacock-Farrell and Jamal Lewis are among a group last selected in November 2025.

Approaching the four-year anniversary of his return to the job, it will be interesting to see whether O'Neill feels his first four-game window forces him to rely more heavily on the depth he has built across this year.

Jersey Bulls Women lost a league game for the first time in their history as they went down 3-0 at Sutton United Under-23s.

The islanders were playing in the Surrey Premier Division of the South East Counties Women's Football League for the first time after winning every game on their way to promotion last season.

The island side had a perfect record as they won the league's Surrey Division One last term in their first season in the English football pyramid.

But they found the step up in level tough as they lost for the second successive game, having been beaten in the FA Cup last week.

After a goalless first half the hosts took the lead within three minutes of the restart when Rachel Marlow flicked on a free kick.

It was 2-0 soon after when Neriyah Anderson-Bailey scored from the edge of the box after a corner before Maya Anderson wrapped up the win.

articles.title: Cristina Librán podría ser la guinda al proyecto del Atlético de Madrid
articles.standfirst: Las rojiblancas intentan cerrar la llegada de la joven centrocampista que actualmente milita en la Juventus
articles.summary: Las rojiblancas intentan cerrar la llegada de la joven centrocampista que actualmente milita en la Juventus
articles.body: El Atlético de Madrid quiere dar un último retoque a su plantilla y apura los últimos días de mercado [en España cierra el próximo viernes a las 23:59 horas] para incorporar alguna jugadora que de un plus a una plantilla renovada. El nombre por el que estaría apostando la dirección deportiva rojiblanca es el de Cristina Librán, centrocampista de 20 años que pertenece a la Juventus de Turín y que actualmente se encuentra en Polonia disputando el Mundial Sub'20. La madrileña, que no ha terminado de cuajar en la Serie A -el año pasado salió cedida al Servette suizo- podría unirse al cuadro dirigido por David González una vez acabe su andadura en su último torneo en las categorías inferiores de la selección donde ya ha sido campeona del mundo Sub'17 y campeona de Europa Sub'19. De momento tiene contrato con la Juventus hasta junio de 2028, pero parece no entrar en los planes de Isaac Guerrero, con quien apenas ha jugado 23 minutos en un amistoso ante el Torreense y 45 en la previa de la Champions League frente al St.Pölten. Librán, jugadora de la cantera del Madrid CFF, podría unirse a la larga lista de fichajes del Atlético de Madrid este verano que ha incluido nombres como los de Jenni Hermoso, Celia Segura, Allegra Poljak, Viola Calligaris, Henrietta Csiszár, Génesis Pérez, Maite Zubieta y Lucía Rodríguez. El Atlético de Madrid ocupa actualmente el noveno puesto de la tabla con tres puntos en tres partidos tras ganar al Alavés (1-0) y perder ante Real Madrid (3-2) y Barcelona (4-2), encuentros en los que a pesar de la derrota dejó una buena imagen. "Tenemos que estar en lo más alto de la tabla, entre los tres primeros, y clasificarnos para la Champions League", confesaba en una entrevista en MARCA la noruega Synne Jensen, actualmente máxima goleadora del torneo con cuatro dianas. La llegada de Librán va encauzada a tener más opciones de alcanzar el objetivo.

articles.title: Las quejas que forzaron la respuesta de la Premier: "Tenemos que volver a casa con esta injusticia"
articles.standfirst: Numerosos analistas, además de jugadores del Manchester United, clamaron contra lo ocurrido en el derbi de Old Trafford
articles.summary: Numerosos analistas, además de jugadores del Manchester United, clamaron contra lo ocurrido en el derbi de Old Trafford
articles.body: El clamor fue mayúsculo. Y no se podía esperar menos por la situación global de lo ocurrido: un gol decisivo en claro fuera de juego que fue concedido, el contexto (un derbi) y el equipo perjudicado... un gigante como el Manchester United. Por eso, horas después de protagonizar cada instante de la parrilla televisiva británica o cada hueco en web de los tabloides digitales, el organismo rector del arbitraje de la Premier se disculpó públicamente con los 'Red Devils'. "Es algo realmente extraño. Reconocerán que se equivocaron", anticipaba ya en 'Sky Sports', durante la trasmisión del partido, un ex mancuniano como Gary Neville. La primera reacción desde organismos oficiales, sin embargo, fue dar por válida la acción de Michael Oliver (árbitro de campo) y Matt Donohue (VAR) sacando una imagen del fuera de juego semiautomático que validaba la posición de Erling Haaland. Pero ese no era el 'kit' de la cuestión. El problema, ignorado por los colegiados, era que Enzo Fernández estaba en 'offside' cuando intentaba rematar de cabeza... forzando la acción defensiva de Lisandro Martínez. Sobre ello, volvió Neville en su podcast cuando vio el tuit oficial del Premier League Match Centre: "Creo que están ignorando la regla. Se están metiendo en un lío aún mayor, me sorprende mucho que hayan publicado eso. Tendrán que retractarse". Y lo hicieron. Pero antes, los propios protagonistas del partido alzaron la voz. "Cada temporada, los directivos de la Premier vienen a nuestro club y dedican una hora a explicarnos las reglas, y se les ve muy seguros de sí mismos al hacerlo. Que después cinco o seis personas cometan este tipo de error en la Premier League es inaceptable. Tenemos que volver a casa con esta injusticia", clamaba Lisandro Martínez. Michael Carrick, técnico del United, tampoco lo entendía: “Es preocupante si así es como el juego es visto por los árbitros. Intentamos ayudar a los árbitros a tomar las decisiones correctas... pero es así como se interpretan las reglas. Decir que Enzo Fernández no interfiere literalmente con el juego está más allá de mí. Es alucinante. Me parece realmente extraño cómo se interpreta eso. No lo podía entender cuando lo vi, y luego la explicación lo hizo peor". Incluso un ex del Manchester City, como Micah Richards, tenía claro que se había cometido un error. "Creo que ha sido un mal día para los árbitros y el VAR. Se equivocaron con la decisión sobre Phil Foden (roja directa) , y también se equivocaron con esta decisión", argumentaba. Además, habló desde la experiencia: "Yo he estado en esa posición como defensa, donde cualquier pequeño movimiento puede marcar la diferencia entre ir a por el balón o no, así que, por supuesto, le afecta". Por todo eso, ante un clamor unánime, el organismo arbitral de la Premier League (Pro Ref, organismo rector del fútbol inglés) admitió justo antes de la medianoche el error al conceder el gol de la victoria al Manchester City (anotado por Erling Haaland) en el 0-1 de Old Trafford, ayer domingo. "Tras el incidente ocurrido en el minuto 60 del partido de la Premier League del domingo entre el Manchester United y el Manchester City en Old Trafford, podemos aclarar la situación respecto al gol concedido a Erling Haaland: La decisión en el terreno de juego fue de fuera de juego contra Erling Haaland; fue revisada por el VAR y se determinó que estaba en posición reglamentaria. En la misma jugada, se determinó que Enzo Fernández no tocó el balón y, por lo tanto, cualquier fuera de juego es subjetivo; sin embargo, en esta ocasión, el VAR no reconoció el probable impacto de su posición y debería haber recomendado una revisión en el terreno de juego. Nos hemos puesto en contacto con el Manchester United esta tarde para reconocer lo que consideramos un error de juicio. Se llevará a cabo una revisión del incidente".

articles.title: Leeds vs Newcastle: Daniel Farke sets out blueprint for success after unbeaten Premier League start
articles.summary: In an exclusive interview with Sky Sports, Daniel Farke explains his desire to take Leeds to new heights and reestablish his side as a Premier League staple; watch Leeds vs Newcastle live on Sky Sports Football on Monday; kick-off 8pm
articles.body:
From the early knockings, it's clear Farke is sticking with his tried and tested formula. A way of working that brought Leeds 47 points and had them in the comfort of safety by April last season.

"It's important to use momentum in the right way," he tells Sky Sports from Leeds' training base. "We needed to freshen blood after a successful season but it's about evolution not revolution". The blueprint is similar with subtle changes: Carry all the good things from the last campaign into this one but do so with added tactical variety.

He wants to keep Newcastle, or any opponent for that matter, guessing before, during and after the game. That is part of the reason why no player in Farke's squad is deemed undroppable. Not even his captain. When pushed on that topic, he says: "It's realistic. You always have to deliver in the best league in the world.

"If you think at any time 'I don't have to do the basics, I'm a superstar' then you are not good enough any more. I'm a big believer in you get what you are willing to invest.

"But if you know yourself to be doing one step less, or working with just 98 per cent, you are not good enough. The culture is more important than any individual. Of course we have outstanding individuals, they have good chances to play every week, but every player has to show the best of themselves every day."

The culture that Farke speaks of is geared toward establishing Leeds as a Premier League mainstay. "We're not addicted to one point per game," he emphasises, another distinction between last season and this. A point-per-game average used to be the yardstick by which Farke measured survival. They are more than just survivors now.

Adaptability is his new watchword. That might mean Leeds fall on the wrong side of certain results while trying to push for more wins, but the risk will be managed. Some demons have already been exorcised away at Nottingham Forest and Brighton, grounds they lost heavily at last year. "We're working on being less predictable. It can be fun, too.

"The DNA has not changed. We want to develop as a team, playing on the front foot with an offensive mind, even against the better teams. The work has been on our tactical flexibility. Now we can change the base formation, so we're not easy to predict."

Farke implemented a tactical tweak that altered the course of last season, switching from a back four to a back three. Extrinsically, it's a shift that was spoken about as a turning point. It followed a groundswell of pressure and unrest around Farke's position. Leeds responded by beating Chelsea and drawing with Liverpool, amid a run that landed them comfortably 14th.

The success of that streak drew praise from Jamie Carragher on Monday Night Football back in May: "I feel like I'm watching an established Premier League team."

Taking greater control in games was another reason for the system switch. "We are preparing a structure in possession for a moment if we lose the ball. The better we are in possession the easier it is to be spot on against the ball, to control the moments the opponent are dangerous.

"We want to have a good structure and be solid in possession." Summer additions James Trafford and Tarik Muharemovic have aided solidity immensely. The aura of confidence radiates from them throughout the spine of the team.

He adds: "The heart of our game has to be control, being stable is very important. It's up to this group to prove we are in a better position than last season, after three games I'm not willing to judge it. It's too early to sing high praises, but we've delivered some quality work in the last month. We have to ride with this moment."

Farke has earned the right to enter games with the aim of being the dominant force. Leeds have only lost one of their last 12 league outings since mid-March. And they thrive at Elland Road. He wants to see a "return to clinical behaviour" against Newcastle, after squandering chances to win at Brighton last week. But no doubt Leeds are harder to beat.

The level has been raised. "In the last 25 years, this club has never managed to play two solid Premier League seasons in a row. I want to do that," he concludes. Early days, but Leeds currently find themselves 11th.

"We are not praying for one point per game. We concentrate on the contents. One day to talk about Europe, to reestablish 'the good old times', would be nice. But we cannot take it for granted. I will make sure we are doing steps in the right direction and then, one day, we will speak about other goals.

"To win the Premier League? I would never say no. But I'm not addicted to the table. I'm addicted to performances and results. That is how it should look."

articles.title: Cristiano Ronaldo: Portugal captain calls for lifetime bans after Diogo Jota chanting aimed at Ruben Neves
articles.summary: Saudi Pro League, Saudi FA, Al Hilal and Al Taawoun clubs have condemned Diogo Jota chanting, with an investigation under way; Ruben Neves says he hopes the supporters "don't go to pray later" after the incident; Cristiano Ronaldo says league "must take action"
articles.body:
Neves was targeted by a section of fans during Al Hilal's 6-0 Saudi Pro League win over Al Taawoun on Saturday, who repeatedly shouted "Jota" at the midfielder.

Jota, the Liverpool forward and former Wolves player, died alongside his brother Andre Silva in a car crash in Spain last July, aged 28.

Neves was a close friend and former team-mate of Jota at both Wolves and with Portugal. He now wears the No 21 shirt for his country in his memory and has a tattoo depicting the pair embracing.

Ronaldo, who plays for Saudi rivals Al Nassr, condemned the chants on social media.

"The league must take action and punish this kind of fan behaviour," Ronaldo wrote.

"This is no longer football, and there have to be limits. People who behave like this should never be allowed to enter a stadium again."

Neves was seen sarcastically applauding the supporters before pointing to the sky during the incident.

After the match, he said: "I just hope they don't go to pray later after what they did."

Both clubs subsequently condemned the behaviour, while the Saudi Arabian Football Federation and Saudi Pro League also issued a joint statement.

The governing bodies described the conduct as "inconsistent with the values of Saudi football and the principles of sportsmanship", adding that using personal tragedies to abuse or provoke others was unacceptable.

The SAFF confirmed its relevant committees had identified the incident and were investigating.

Jota joined Liverpool from Wolves in 2020 and scored 65 goals in 182 appearances for the club. He also scored 14 times in 49 Portugal appearances after making his international debut in 2019.

articles.title: Erling Haaland's goal for Man City against Man Utd was a mistake- but why did it happen?
articles.summary: Sky Sports' answers the key questions following Erling Haaland's controversial winner in the Manchester derby; Man City won 1-0 at Old Trafford and refereeing body Pro Ref admitted to an "error of judgment" in awarding the goal
articles.body:
The striker's goal was initially disallowed for offside on the pitch before VAR overturned the decision.

The VAR officials deemed that Haaland was played onside by Manchester United defender Patrick Dorgu. However, Manchester City's Enzo Fernandez was in an offside position as he attempted to play the ball before it reached Haaland.

Here, we look at some of the key questions surrounding the incident...

Have Pro Ref explained why the goal was awarded?

Pro Ref - the Professional Game Referees formerly known as the PGMOL or PGMO - confirmed on Sunday night that a mistake was made when City's winning goal was awarded.

While acknowledging "an error of judgement", their statement only offered a partial explanation for why the goal was mistakenly awarded.

Having admitted the goal should have remained ruled out because Fernandez was offside, the statement declared: "On this occasion, the VAR did not recognise the likely impact of his position."

But the overarching question of why the VAR failed to appreciate that a player in an offside position six yards from goal, making a diving header for a ball between two opponents, was not judged to have either impacted play or potentially impacted play remains unanswered.

Could the mistake have happened because the VAR was focused on whether Fernandez played the ball?

This, currently, appears to be the most logical explanation.

In their mid-game post on X explaining the decision, Match Centre wrote: "The VAR also deemed that while in an offside position, Fernandez didn't play the ball."

During Sky Sports' match coverage, replays were also shown of the VAR team apparently scrutinising whether or not Fernandez touched the ball as it flew across the six-yard box.

So was it the case that the VAR became distracted by fixating on a technicality that didn't actually matter given the offside rule clearly stipulates that a player can be offside regardless of whether or not he touches the ball?

Why did the Pro Ref statement say the goal should have been sent for an on-field review?

According to Pro Ref, the initial offside decision was made against Erling Haaland. He, though, was onside.

The review then moved on to Fernandez, who was correctly deemed to be in an offside position by the VAR team.

The problem was that they then apparently, and incorrectly, focused entirely on whether he touched the ball.

What the VAR couldn't do, however, was confirm the goal was rightly ruled out - for the Fernandez offside - for the wrong reason - the Haaland offside.

Hence Pro Ref's assertion that the VAR ought to have requested referee Michael Oliver make an on-field review in which Oliver would have been asked to make a subjective decision on whether Fernandez impacted play.

Yes. Replays of Haaland's goal also show the Manchester United goalkeeper made an initial reaction to Fernandez, raising his arms in anticipation of a header and shifting off balance for when Haaland struck the ball.

But Martinez had already been impacted by Fernandez's position, so the goal should have been disallowed regardless of whether Lammens was distracted by Fernandez's attempt to play the ball.

Yes and no - the yes because the offside was given against an onside player, the no because the goal should have been ruled out for offside.

So the VAR couldn't have definitively ruled out the goal?

No. Because the on-field decision was against Haaland, the only course of action, if the process was followed to the letter, was to ask the referee to make an on-field review.

While Donohue has only ever refereed four Premier League games, he has substantial experience as a VAR. In 2025/26, he was the VAR for 24 Premier League matches and six as Assistant VAR.

Why didn't TV viewers see offside lines drawn during the game?

The Premier League is using semi-automated offside technology this season which provides a kick-point graphic for incidents under review.

This is different to the previous process in which the VAR teams would manually place crosshairs to determine offside calls and then draw lines.

Did the officials also forget they made a VAR check?

One final unanswered question from Manchester's derby is whether the officials also forgot about the VAR check when determining how much added-on time to play at the end of the game.

Haaland's goal was scored after 59 minutes and 24 seconds. Following the lengthy review, play didn't restart until 63 minutes and 15 seconds. But despite that delay, and numerous others during the course of the half, just five minutes were added on.

articles.title: Lamine Yamal says he ‘deserves’ Ballon d’Or but Mbappe his main rival
articles.summary: ‘Mbappe and I are the two best in the world,’ Yamal says before claiming he’d deserve to win the prestigious award.
articles.body:
Lamine Yamal believes he would be a deserved winner of the Ballon d’Or this year, given his World Cup success with Spain and La Liga glory with Barcelona , but his closest competitor for the prestigious football award would be Real Madrid rival Kylian Mbappe.

“I honestly believe there are two of us who are the best in the world, and this year I’d deserve it because of what I’ve won,” Lamine said in an interview clip shared by Spanish streaming platform Movistar on Sunday.

“As far as I’m concerned, Mbappe and I are the two best in the world. It’s clear to me, and everyone who watches the matches knows it.”

France striker Mbappe was the top scorer at the World Cup as well as in La Liga and the Champions League, and said last week no player was better than him last season, though he failed to win any silverware.

Yamal was named La Liga’s best player in 2025-26 as Barcelona successfully defended the title, and later played a key role in Spain winning the World Cup in North America.

He had struck a more measured tone at a news conference last Tuesday, saying he believed he had a chance after an “incredible” season but would not beg for votes.

Mbappe, meanwhile, has also made his case for the award in recent days.

The Spanish teen was runner-up to Ousmane Dembele last year, while Mbappe was third in 2023, when Lionel Messi won the award for a record eighth time.

Dembele believes the award should remain with a Paris Saint-Germain player after the French club retained the Champions League.

Bayern Munich striker and England international Harry Kane is also among the favourites to win the award, which will be presented in London on October 26.

articles.title: Time for Sebastien Pocognoli to pick - who could be named in new-look Scotland squad?
articles.summary: Sebastien Pocognoli will name his first Scotland squad on Tuesday, but what can we expect? Will the new head coach use this clean slate as time to call upon new names? BBC Sport Scotland takes a look at the potential candidates...
articles.body:
On Tuesday, Sebastien Pocognoli will name his first squad since being appointed the national team's head coach for the upcoming Nations League B fixtures.

His predecessor, Steve Clarke, prioritised consistency in his squad during his successful seven-year reign, which ultimately culminated in a first men's World Cup appearance in 28 years.

But his loyalty was often viewed - from supporters at least - as his biggest downfall, with regular calls for fresh faces often unanswered.

Now, if ever, feels the time for such hopes to be heard.

But, will the Belgian make sweeping changes from the experienced squad who returned from the United States earlier than planned? Or will continuity be key for matches against Slovenia, Switzerland and North Macedonia?

The Tartan Army will certainly be hoping for the former, and BBC Scotland takes a look at some uncapped and out-of-the-frame players who could be in line for a call-up.

Irvine stays as Pocognoli refreshes Scotland staff

What awaits new Scotland head coach Pocognoli?

Youthful Pocognoli the brave choice for Scotland job

Is McFarlane the long-term answer to sticky situation in goal?

A problem area for the latter years of Clarke's reign will remain a problem area in the early Pocognoli days.

Angus Gunn started between the sticks at the World Cup and, though he has found more regular football in the States since joining San Jose Earthquakes, he has conceded a rather alarming 21 goals in nine Major League Soccer games - though he did make four decent stops in San Jose's win on Thursday.

He was joined at the major tournament by Craig Gordon - who has since retired from football - and Liam Kelly, who has not featured since Derek McInnes took over at Rangers in the summer, suggesting there could be two goalkeeping spots up for grabs in this squad.

Scott Bain could have felt a little hard done by not making the trip across the pond in June, given he was playing regular Scottish Premiership football with Falkirk and picked up his fourth cap against Ivory Coast in April.

He's made a steady start to his season - recovering from an error against Celtic to pulling off a string of impressive saves against Dundee United - with his Bairns boss John McGlynn recently tipping him to start for Scotland later this month.

Liam McFarlane may not be challenging him for a starting berth, but the 21-year-old must be well-placed for a call-up as the third-choice shotstopper.

Since joining Partick Thistle in the summer on loan from Hearts - after being stateside as the training goalkeeper in Clarke's World Cup squad - he has conceded just one goal in five Championship games and is well thought of by both club and country.

Given the sticky situation the Scots have found themselves in this department in recent times, surely including the youngster sooner rather than later with a look to the future is a step in the right direction.

Is Bain on course to be Scotland's number one?

Will there be a changing of the (rear)guard?

Continuing on that theme, there could be a bit of a changing of the guard in the rest of the rearguard too.

Grant Hanley, 34, limped off in Hibernian's recent defeat by St Johnstone and John Souttar, 29, has not been included in any matchday squad for Rangers this term - amid interest from abroad.

Following his mighty impressive season on-loan at Motherwell last year, ex-Celtic centre-half Stephen Welsh has taken to life in England's Championship with Swansea like a duck to water, reigniting calls for his inclusion in the squad.

A former under-21s captain, the 26-year-old recently got the better of a fellow potential new cap in Stoke City's Luke Graham .

The former Dundee defender made the switch to The Potters after being involved in the A-squad's training before the World Cup and on the bench for the Curacao friendly.

Strong in the air and left-footed, Graham appears a direct competitor for Scott McKenna - as does Luis Binks .

Perhaps a more unfamiliar name, the 25-year-old captains Danish Superliga side Brondby and previously represented the Scots at under-18 level before playing for England youth.

In a fascinating and revealing interview , external last month - where he encouraged young Scottish players to remain in their homeland rather than become "a number" in England - the former Spurs youth product - who calls Aaron Hickey a pal from their Bologna days - spoke of his desire for a Scotland call-up, despite never having had that conversation with Clarke.

Since that article dropped in August, the clamour online for his inclusion has rocketed and it very much appears the ball is in Scotland - and Pocognoli's - court.

There has also been a fair bit of discourse surrounding Colby Donovan , who has been flung into Celtic's starting side in Alistair Johnston's absence - notably in front of World Cup squad member, Anthony Ralston.

It appears a matter of when, not if, the 20-year-old right-back will make the first team but he has stiff competition with fellow youngsters Hickey, Nathan Patterson and Max Johnston.

One could even throw in left-back Josh Doig to that pile too. The Sassuolo defender is another in line for a recall.

Will Miller & Mulligan challenge returning Gilmour?

Returning from the knee injury he sustained on the eve of the Scots' flight to Florida, Billy Gilmour will almost certainly be included in Pocognoli's squad.

The midfielder lasted the duration of Napoli's opening Champions League match in the defeat by Arsenal last week, after coming off the bench against Inter Milan in Serie A days before.

His presence was missed stateside but hopes will be high for Gilmour to be at the heart of his country's next chapter.

Many thought Lennon Miller would take his seat on the plane, but Tyler Fletcher timed his run perfectly for that.

Things have not quite yet gone to plan for the 20-year-old at Udinese, as he struggles to break into the Serie A side's starting XI but with Scott McTominay recovering from heart surgery, the former Motherwell man might be given the chance to add to his four caps.

Hibernian's Josh Mulligan might also be in with a shout, despite his side's sticky start to the season.

Involved in the international set-up last year, the 23-year-old is yet to be capped but did impress in the Edinburgh derby Pocognoli attended earlier this month and has been one of the brightest and most consistent performers for David Gray's struggling Hibs side.

McTominay's heart procedure 'a complete success'

Who can capitalise on Shankland's absence?

Speaking of struggles, Scotland still seem to lack that genuine, top class, goalscoring striker.

Che Adams appears to be a shoo-in - not least because he has two goals in three Serie A games for Torino - but who else joins him is a little less certain.

Rangers captain Lawrence Shankland is out injured , and at 30-years-old, Pocognoli now may feel the time to rely on Millwall's Lyndon Dykes is nearing an end.

Throughout the calendar year, there has been a real will-they, won't-they dance with Scotland and Oli McBurnie .

It appeared fairly clear under Clarke - who was unimpressed a private conversation between the pair was shared - that the Hull City striker would not be returning to his squad for the first time since 2021, but the Belgian may be willing to offer a clean slate.

Though he has not yet scored this season for the Tigers - who sit third in the Premier League - the towering and tough 30-year-old is their star striker and put in a tremendous performance as they mauled Manchester United , before setting up the second in their 2-2 draw with Chelsea at Stamford Bridge on Saturday.

Can Pocognoli afford to continue McBurnie's Scotland exile?

Is Sevilla's 'all-round striker' Ure ready to lead Scotland's attack?

While Scotland didn't spend nearly as much of their summer in the States as hoped, one Scotman's name certainly dominated the discourse during July and August: Robbie Ure.

The Rangers academy product was in demand across Europe after a free-scoring spell with Sirius in Sweden - 20 goals and three assists in 20 matches - and it resulted in a £5.5m move to La Liga giants Sevilla.

The 22-year-old has yet to put on his shooting boots in Spain but, given his eligibility for Ukraine, Pocognoli might be tempted to tie him down as soon as possible.

Also on the move in the summer was Kieron Bowie .

After his Hellas Verona side were relegated from Italy's top tier, he teamed up with Doig at Sassuolo and impressed, even before he opened his account in the dramatic victory over Juventus on Sunday - sparking wild scenes as he netted his second career goal against the Old Lady.

His attributes are clear. A strong, physical forward with a powerful left foot, he will be hopeful of adding to his two caps.

Will all three of Hearts' frontline make squad?

From on the continent to closer to home, there is a strong case Hearts head coach Wouter Vrancken’s preferred front three make this squad.

Leading the line is already-capped James Wilson , who appears a player reinvigorated following his loan spell with Tottenham Hotspur youths last season.

Another goal against Hibs - in front of the Belgian - ought to have done wonders for the teenager, who has started the season like a buoyant boy with something to prove.

He has been helped in no small part, though, by wide men Calvin Miller and Josh McPake .

The latter‘s goal at Easter Road sparked wild scenes in the away end as he announced himself as a serious contender for a call-up - if his performances in the Championship last year with title-winning St Johnstone were not convincing enough.

Another star who took his second-tier form into the top flight is Miller, who has - like McPake - immersed himself in the free-flowing football Pocognoli’s countryman Vrancken likes to play.

The clamour for the trio’s call-up is captivating, whether the new Scotland head coach pays attention to it, is another matter.

A big auld pool for Pocognoli to ponder from.
